question.problem:
$$
(\,∀x\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{I}\end{aligned}}<y\,)⇒(\,∃z\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{II}\end{aligned}}<{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{III}\end{aligned}}<y\,)
$$

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
question.worked_solution:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\text{b})$ or free $(\text{f}).$

- Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∀x$ that uses $x:$

$$
(\,∀x\in R,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∀x}{\overset{⏞}{{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}<y}}\,)⇒(\,∃z\in R,\,x<z<y\,)
$$

- Occurrence II of the variable $x$ is *free* since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

- Occurrence III of the variable $z$ is *bound* since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $∃$ that uses $z:$ 

$$
(\,∀x\in R,\,x<1\,)⇒(\,∃z\in R,\,\overset{\text{scope of }∀z}{\overset{⏞}{x<{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}<y}}\,)
$$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows:

$$
(\,∀{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}<{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}\,)⇒(\,∃{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}\in R,\,{x}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}<{z}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{b}\end{aligned}}<{y}_{\begin{aligned} \\ ↑ \\ \text{f}\end{aligned}}\,)
$$

Therefore, the free occurrence is "II only."
